name: Baylor University
header:
Baylor University
United States · Mathematics PhD
Roster and rank verification handled separately
Eligibility and preparation · Deadlines by stage · English and GRE · Academic records · Recommendation letters · Written
materials · Funding and fees · Conflicts and remaining checks · Faculty · Sources
Pay attention to
• Baylor is retained as an additional program if the final ranking roster places it outside the top-100 boundary.
• Submission cutoff is 10:59 p.m. CST.
• The short mathematics checklist omits writing requirements found in the older central handbook.

sections.title: Eligibility and preparation
sections.text:
Eligibility for your route [Standing rule]
Direct admission from a mathematics bachelor’s degree is explicitly allowed and is the usual route. Baylor
mathematics admits PhD applicants, not students seeking only a standalone master’s. Strong proof-based
analysis and algebra preparation matters. [s1] [s2]
Before submission [Standing rule]
Use the Graduate School application, arrange three references, upload records from all institutions, prepare a
CV/résumé and personal statement, and resolve English testing or the waiver. The CV/statement requirement
is explicit in the 2024-25 central handbook but omitted from the short department checklist; verify the current
mathematics portal. [s1] [s3] [s4] [s6]
Adviser contact [Standing rule]
No prior supervisor agreement is listed. Representation theory provides the clearest verified fit; contact current
graduate faculty about capacity. The current group lists Hunziker and Wilbert, whose Baylor appointment
began August 2026. [s1] [s7] [s9] [s11]
Portal workflow [Standing rule]
Application status can be checked through the online application. The older handbook illustrates an applicant
checklist, but the current letter-specific receipt display and notifications were not independently established.
[s3] [s6]
Cycle verification [Standing rule]
Standing mathematics rules and current 2026 faculty/funding pages were checked November 5, 2026. The
publicly available administrative handbook is 2024-25 and is explicitly treated as historical evidence where
used. [s1] [s2] [s6] [s9]

sections.title: Deadlines by stage
sections.text:
Academic application; Funding consideration [Standing rule]
December 15 is the standing mathematics deadline. Central instructions specify submission by 10:59 p.m.
Central Standard Time for receipt on that date. The general Graduate School February date does not supersede
the earlier mathematics deadline. No explicitly labelled Fall 2027 mathematics date was established. [s1] [s3]
[s5]
Reference receipt; Supporting documents [Standing rule]
Have the three recommendations and supporting records complete for the December 15 mathematics
deadline. No separate later recommendation/document cutoff was established. Any exception for a late or
incomplete application requires the program’s agreement. [s1] [s3]

Test-score receipt [Standing rule]
Required English scores or a processed waiver are needed for official review; required tests must be
uploaded/reported as the portal directs. General GRE is optional for mathematics, so the central rule blocking
submission without a required GRE report should not be interpreted as a mathematics GRE mandate. No
distinct later score deadline was established. [s2] [s3] [s4]
Accepting an offer [Standing rule]
The central FAQ states an April 15 response rule for fall financial-support offers. Confirm this standing rule and
any interim requirements in the actual Fall 2027 offer. [s3]

sections.title: English and GRE
sections.text:
English requirement [Standing rule]
For doctoral applicants, current central minimums are TOEFL 4.5 on the new scale, IELTS 6.5 or Duolingo 125;
scores have a two-year validity period. The mathematics FAQ says it generally likes at least 90 on the former
TOEFL scale. ETS code: 6032. [s2] [s4]
UChicago English exemption [Standing rule]
A conferred degree from a US institution qualifies. Upload the transcript and email
GraduateAdmissions@baylor.edu to request the waiver. Central rules also allow a conferred degree taught
entirely in English with acceptable evidence. Whether a still-pending UChicago degree can obtain the waiver
before the application deadline is not established. [s2] [s3] [s4]
GRE General [Standing rule]
Optional according to the mathematics FAQ; no public preference or prohibition was stated. [s2]
GRE Mathematics [Standing rule]
Not required according to the mathematics FAQ. The page does not establish whether submitting a strong
score is preferred or how it is weighted. [s2]

Transcripts and degree records [Standing rule]
Unofficial transcripts from every academic institution attended are required initially. Official transcripts with
degree conferral follow admission and are due by the first day of classes; arrange institutional electronic
delivery to Grad_Transcripts@baylor.edu or sealed official delivery. [s1] [s3] [s6]
Mathematics-course list; Course descriptions [Standing rule]
Not listed as a separate required item on the public mathematics application checklist. This does not establish
whether the current portal permits an optional upload; exact prompt, length, formatting and upload/link rule
are not published. [s1]

sections.title: Recommendation letters
sections.text:
Number and type [Standing rule]
Three recommendations are required. The older central handbook asks for names, titles and contact details
and allows a personal message to each recommender. [s1] [s6]
Scholarship references [Standing rule]
All accepted mathematics students receive the standard assistantship; no separate standard funding essay or
additional referee is listed. Award-specific extra requirements were not established. [s1] [s2]
What sends the invitation; Before versus after submission [Prior cycle]
The 2024-25 central handbook says entering names/contact information is followed by an automated Slate
invitation containing an upload link. It does not explicitly establish the precise save button or whether a current

submission prerequisite exists. Recommenders may also email GraduateAdmissions@baylor.edu. Confirm the
current trigger in the portal. [s6]
Receipt confirmation [Standing rule]
Application status can be checked through the online application. The older handbook illustrates an applicant
checklist, but the current letter-specific receipt display and notifications were not independently established.
[s3] [s6]
Updating and reusing letters [Standing rule]
The central FAQ allows requesting transfer of previous application materials within two years after submitting a
new application and fee. Email GraduateAdmissions@baylor.edu with identifying information, program, degree,
entry term and the items requested. Confirm individual letters and any updated replacement directly; no
universal self-service replacement rule was established. [s3]

sections.title: Funding and fees
sections.text:
Amount and coverage [Standing rule]
The mathematics FAQ advertises $33,000 for twelve months, plus a $2,000 first-year moving supplement, full
tuition, no general student fees, conference travel and an 80% student health-insurance subsidy. These are
current standing advertised terms, not an individually issued Fall 2027 award. [s2]
Years of support [Standing rule]
The program allows five years of graduate study. The FAQ does not separately state a legally guaranteed
five-year funding term or all renewal conditions; verify them in the offer. [s2]
International eligibility [Standing rule]
The department says all accepted students receive an assistantship, without excluding international
applicants, and explicitly discusses international admission. Confirm any English teaching certification and
individual appointment conditions. [s2]
Conditions and duties [Standing rule]
From the second year onward, students typically teach one undergraduate course each semester. The
department advertises support for two conferences annually. Annual academic-progress, employment and
insurance terms should be checked in the award. [s2]

Extra funding application [Standing rule]
All accepted mathematics students receive the standard assistantship; no separate standard funding essay or
additional referee is listed. Award-specific extra requirements were not established. [s1] [s2]
Other funding routes [Unresolved]
The central FAQ directs applicants to departmental and non-academic assistantships and outside funding
resources. Specific additional mathematics awards, international eligibility, amounts and separate essays were
not established. [s3]
Application fee [Conflict]
Central admissions charges international applicants $60; the mathematics checklist still quotes $50 without
distinguishing citizenship. Budget $60 and verify the checkout amount. [s1] [s3]
Fee waiver [Standing rule]
The central FAQ identifies active/retired US military and McNair Scholars for a waiver of the domestic fee. No
general financial-hardship waiver or automatic waiver for an F-1 UChicago student was established; ask before
paying if an affiliation applies. [s3]

sections.title: Conflicts and remaining checks
sections.text:
Conflicting sources [Conflict]
The department’s $50 fee conflicts with the central $60 international fee. Its short checklist omits CV/personal
statement requirements that are explicit in the older central handbook. The old TOEFL preference and current
new-scale minimum are different types of information, not interchangeable thresholds. [s1] [s2] [s3] [s4] [s6]
Checks still needed [Unresolved]
Confirm Fall 2027 mathematics date, in-progress UChicago English waiver, current CV/statement prompts and
formatting, exact referee invitation/receipt/replacement mechanics, and funding renewal terms. [s1] [s3] [s4] [s6]

sections.title: Potential advisers and recent research
sections.text:
Representation theory / algebraic geometry
Markus Hunziker
Lie-group representations, invariant theory and covariants, highest-weight modules, and associated algebraic
geometry and combinatorics. [s7] [s8]
Listed on official departmental faculty pages; availability to supervise new PhD students is not published.
Research evidence: 2026 · Stanley decompositions of modules of covariants
Recent research evidence; verify supervision availability separately.
Geometric representation theory
Arik Wilbert
Springer varieties, geometric and combinatorial representation theory, categorification, and connections to
low-dimensional topology. [s7] [s9] [s10]
Assistant Professor at Baylor since August 2026. Older South Alabama pages are obsolete for current affiliation; supervision
availability is not published.
Research evidence: 2025 · Two-row Delta Springer varieties
Recent research evidence; verify supervision availability separately.
